records.name: Baltazaras
records.facts_used: The dictionary pairs Baltazaras with Balthasar, a variant in the Balthazar/Belshazzar family. Balthazar is traditionally one of the Magi’s names; that personal name belongs to later tradition, rather than the Gospel’s account of their visit. The exact form is documented in the Senn–Salys Lithuanian–German dictionary of 1968, reprinted in Salys’s collected writings in 1983. This is a dated linguistic record of the name and its relationships; it does not identify the first child registered with this spelling.

records.name: Merkelis
records.facts_used: Salys’s historical calendar explicitly gives Merkelis as a short form of Melchioras. This is a documented Lithuanian full-name relationship; it does not depend on interpreting the letters of Merkelis as separate Lithuanian words. A historical bearer was Merkelis Giedraitis, born about 1536, bishop of Samogitia from 1576. He financed Daukša’s Lithuanian Postilė of 1599. The 1964 calendar later prints Melchioras (Merkelis) on 6 January; it is not the name’s first use.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.

records.name: Aabel
records.facts_used: Rajandi directs Aabel to Abel and Hebrew Hevel. He calls the original meaning uncertain, distinguishing later explanations involving breath, vapour and transience. The popular claim that Aabel is simply a short form of Abraham is not his analysis. The form and its relationships are documented in Edgar Rajandi’s Raamat nimedest, published in Tallinn in 1966. The book records the naming traditions known at that time. Its publication date documents a linguistic treatment, rather than the name’s invention or its first birth registration.
